title: City centre: a daily charge for cars
question: What could happen if the city of Harrowgate introduces a daily charge for cars entering its centre?

documents.name: 01-council-transport-report.md
documents.content:
# Council transport report: a central charge

This is a fictional report written for an evaluation. All names, places and figures are invented.

## Proposal

Harrowgate City Council proposes a daily charge of £6 for cars entering the central zone between 7am and 7pm on weekdays, starting in January. Revenue would be used only to improve bus services.

## Traffic

Counts show that 52,000 vehicles a day enter the central zone. The council expects the charge to reduce car entries by about one in six.

## Process

A traffic regulation order is required before any charge can start, and it needs a public consultation of at least six weeks. Camera and plate-recognition equipment would take nine months to procure and install.

## Data

Images of number plates may be kept for no more than 30 days under the council's data policy.

documents.name: 02-traders-and-access-note.md
documents.content:
# Traders and access note

This is a fictional note written for an evaluation. All names, places and figures are invented.

## Traders

The Harrowgate Traders' Association says that city-centre shops will lose trade, and points to a nearby town where footfall fell after a similar charge. The association asks for free parking in the council's car parks for the first two hours.

## Access

Residents of the central zone would be offered a 90% discount. Blue badge holders would be exempt. The disability access group asked that taxis used by disabled people be exempt too, and said that the bus stops on the main road are not step-free.

## Buses

The bus operator says it can add routes only when new buses are delivered, which takes about a year, and that bus lanes need the council to act.

documents.name: 03-air-quality-and-counts.md
documents.content:
# Air quality and counts

This is a fictional note written for an evaluation. All names, places and figures are invented.

## Air quality

The air quality monitor on the main road recorded levels above the legal limit on 41 days last year. The health authority says that the limit protects children and older people.

## Counts

The traffic team's counts show that 47,000 vehicles a day enter the central zone. Delivery vans make up about 15% of those vehicles.

## Neighbouring areas

Residents of streets just outside the zone fear that drivers would park there to avoid the charge.
